body: I now have a local repo where I can reproduce it every time. The repo is quite large (~10 GB packed), so am open to running inspection queries or suggestions how to convert it into a minimally reproducible example.

Thanks for reporting this, @borancar and thanks for the clarifying error PR https://github.com/gkgoat1.

b/150301500 doesn't have much other insight beyond Googler user reports. The two other relevant comments on that bug are:

 - @janakdr : "looks like this can happen when a target in error has already declared a dep. That means there's an edge there to traverse, but no configured target on the other end of it." 
 - @gregestren - struggling to reproduce any of the failures (although @janakdr showed a reproduction on Google's repo I can try to replicate).

So the short story is, yes, getting a consistent reproduction is key to addressing this. I'd love a more minimal one from you @borancar but I'm not sure what to suggest to help you minimize it?

@sgowroji https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/labels/cquery_aspects is specifically for deficiencies in cquery + [aspect](https://bazel.build/rules/aspects) support. I don't believe aspects are a part of this report?

@borancar does your reproduction repo have any loading/analysis errors in it?

Note, by the way, that contents of source files are not relevant for cquery, only BUILD/bzl files, and existence of some source files (ones consumed by globs), so there's probably a hacky way to get it smaller, although that's probably not the direction to expend our efforts in.

### Description of the bug:


The following steps seem to consistently result in an internal Bazel error:

1. Run a Bazel AQuery //...
2. Delete a file which is an input to a target using a glob.
3. Run a Bazel CQuery rdeps.

There also needs to be an aspect in the workspace.

### What's the simplest, easiest way to reproduce this bug? Please provide a minimal example if possible.


A minimal example that reproduces the error is provided here https://github.com/alexander-scott/bazel_bug_reproduce_1. It has a shell script [`break_bazel.sh`](https://github.com/alexander-scott/bazel_bug_reproduce_1/blob/main/break_bazel.sh) that performs the steps that cause the error.

The shell script does the following:

```
touch glob_scenario/2_test.cpp
bazel aquery //...
rm glob_scenario/2_test.cpp
bazel cquery  -- 'rdeps(//..., //...)'
```

To reproduce this error you can run the following:

```
git clone https://github.com/alexander-scott/bazel_bug_reproduce_1.git
cd bazel_bug_reproduce_1
./break_bazel.sh
```

body: Got a nice small repro from https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/issues/15380 (Bazel 5.1.1. for me). Adding `--noinclude_aspects` to the cquery call removes the crash (but that's not a suggested workaround since that reduces results).

This is happening for me without aspects. I put together a fairly minimal repro here: https://github.com/JamesMBartlett/bazel_fatal_repro.

Running `./fail.sh` in that repo should fail with a very similar error to the above. Interestingly, if I remove either the `--action_env=HOME` in the .bazelrc or the `bazel info execution_root` in `fail.sh`, I no longer see the error.

(edit: I'm on bazel 6.0.0 fyi)
(edit: I also noticed that the configured target that it fails to find, should've been filtered out by the build_tag_filters)
